title: stapler-squad: client network and WebSocket
description: Browser-reported RPC/WebSocket/page-load telemetry (POST /api/analytics -> client_* metrics) next to the server's ws_unary_* metrics. Answers: are unary-over-WS calls timing out, is the browser fanning out or duplicating requests, and which pages load slowly. Client metric sources and label bounds: docs/reference/client-network-telemetry.md.

links.title: Traces in Tempo (Explore)
links.tooltip: Open Grafana Explore on Tempo with this dashboard's time range

panels.title: RPC rate (all tabs)
panels.description: Unary RPCs started per second as seen by the browser, after coalescing (one coalesced flight = one call).

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: Share of calls that ended in a Connect error code. Excludes canceled (navigation and unmount aborts are normal); the Errors row shows those too.

links.title: Errored server spans for the selected methods in Tempo (Explore)

panels.title: Timeout rate
panels.description: deadline_exceeded / all calls.

links.title: Deadline-exceeded server spans for the selected methods in Tempo (Explore)

panels.title: p95 duration
panels.description: Includes browser connection queueing and WS send queueing.

links.title: Slow server spans (> 500ms) for the selected methods in Tempo (Explore)

panels.title: Coalescing misses (share of calls)
panels.description: Coalescible reads started while an identical one was in flight on the shared transport: coalescing should have merged them (flag off, differing priority, or a stale generation). Non-coalescible duplicates are on the Concurrency row.

panels.title: WS fallback to HTTP
panels.description: Unary calls that wanted WebSocket but ran over HTTP (breaker open, call timeout, ...).

panels.title: RPC latency by method and transport
Latency p50 / p95 / p99 (all selected)
panels.description: Round numbers (8000 = WS call timeout, 30000 = default deadline) mean you are looking at timeouts, not slow work.

panels.title: p95 by transport
panels.description: ws = unary WebSocket bridge, http = plain fetch, batch = /batch/unary.

links.title: Slow server spans (> 500ms) for this method in Tempo (Explore)

targets.expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(client_rpc_duration_milliseconds_bucket{method=~"$method",transport=~"$transport"}[$__rate_interval])) by (le, method))) and on(method) topk(8, sum by (method) (rate(client_rpc_duration_milliseconds_count{method=~"$method",transport=~"$transport"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Request rate by method (top 10)
panels.description: A method with an unexpectedly high rate is fan-out: compare with the duplicate panel below.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(client_rpc_duration_milliseconds_count{method=~"$method",transport=~"$transport"}[$__rate_interval])) by (method)) and on(method) topk(10, sum by (method) (rate(client_rpc_duration_milliseconds_count{method=~"$method",transport=~"$transport"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Browser network queue delay p95 (HTTP/1.1 6-connection cap)
panels.description: Time between fetch start and bytes on the wire. High while server latency is low = browser connection starvation.

panels.title: Non-ok calls by Connect code
panels.description: Full Connect code, all methods and transports (the code is not on the per-method histogram, to keep series bounded; see the Timeouts and Error ratio panels for per-method slices).

links.title: Deadline-exceeded server spans for this method in Tempo (Explore)

panels.title: Error ratio by transport
panels.description: Excludes canceled (navigation/unmount aborts are normal).

panels.title: In-flight RPCs at call start (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Calls already in flight in the tab when a new one started (module-wide counter: includes stream calls until their headers arrive and calls on the non-shared transport). Sustained p95 near 6 on http = HTTP/1.1 per-origin connection cap.

panels.title: Duplicate in-flight calls by method
panels.description: Identical read already in flight when this one started. coalescible=false: the method is not coalescible, so these are candidates to add to the set or to de-dup at the call site. coalescible=true: coalescing missed it.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(client_rpc_duplicate_inflight_total{method=~"$method"}[$__rate_interval])) by (method, coalescible)) and on(method) topk(10, sum by (method) (rate(client_rpc_duplicate_inflight_total[$__range])))

panels.title: Coalescing: share of coalescible calls saved
panels.description: joined / (joined + flights started) for the methods that coalesced at least once. Flights started are the rpc.* counts; only joins are beaconed.

targets.expr: sum(rate(client_rpc_coalesce_total[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum(rate(client_rpc_coalesce_total[$__rate_interval])) + sum(sum by (method) (rate(client_rpc_duration_milliseconds_count{transport!="stream"}[$__rate_interval])) and on(method) sum by (method) (rate(client_rpc_coalesce_total[$__rate_interval]))), 1e-9)

panels.title: Calls saved by coalescing, by method (top 10)

targets.expr: (sum(rate(client_rpc_coalesce_total[$__rate_interval])) by (method)) and on(method) topk(10, sum by (method) (rate(client_rpc_coalesce_total[$__range])))

panels.title: Batch size p50 / p95 and fallbacks
panels.description: Calls per /batch/unary request (flag batch_unary). Size near 1 means batching is not collapsing anything.

panels.title: Batch fallbacks by reason
panels.description: request-failed = the whole batch request failed; server-declined = server asked the client to run that member individually.

panels.title: Browser socket events by kind/event
panels.description: Reconnect storms show up as open/close/reconnect all rising together.

panels.title: Browser close codes
panels.description: 1006 = abnormal (network drop/server gone), 1001 = going away, 1000 = normal, 1009 = frame too big, none = browser gave no code.

panels.title: Unary WS call: p95 RTT (browser) vs server handling
panels.description: The gap between the two is queueing + network + socket write.

panels.title: Send queue delay (frame submit -> socket write) p50 / p95
panels.description: Non-zero p95 = calls waiting for the socket to open or for an in-flight slot (backpressure).

panels.title: Pending WS calls when a call is submitted p50 / p95
panels.description: Queue depth the call found: sent-unanswered + queued.

panels.title: Server: connections closed by reason
panels.description: peer_close = browser closed; read_error = socket died/deadline; write_error / ping_failed = server could not write; protocol = bad frame; shutdown = server ended it.

panels.title: Server: ping->pong RTT p50 / p95
panels.description: Browser-tab responsiveness as seen by the server; high with low network latency = throttled/frozen tab.

panels.title: Server: unary WS calls by Connect code
Server: handling time p95 by method (top 8)

targets.expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(ws_unary_call_duration_milliseconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])) by (le, method))) and on(method) topk(8, sum by (method) (rate(ws_unary_call_duration_milliseconds_count[$__range])))

panels.title: Server: zombie handlers (abandoned, still running)
panels.description: A zombie is a handler still running after its call was cancelled/timed out and its slot released. A rising line means handlers that ignore their context.

panels.title: Server: calls abandoned by reason
panels.description: cancel = client CANCEL, deadline = call deadline hit, shutdown = socket ended, zombie_cap = too many zombies closed the socket.

panels.title: Server: upgrades refused by listener and reason
panels.description: origin / auth_required / query / no_listener refusals at the WebSocket upgrade; a browser then falls back to HTTP.

panels.title: Slow page loads and main-thread jank
LCP p75 by page (ms)
panels.description: Core Web Vitals threshold: 2500 good, 4000 poor.

panels.title: INP p75 by page (ms)
panels.description: Thresholds: 200 good, 500 poor.

panels.title: CLS p75 by page
panels.description: Thresholds: 0.1 good, 0.25 poor.

panels.title: Long tasks (>50ms) per minute by page
panels.description: Capped at 30 events/min per tab at the source, so a saturated line means 'at least this janky'.

panels.title: Beacon health: events the server rejected
panels.description: Non-zero means a client sent an event the allow-list refused (version skew or a bug).

panels.title: Server-side RPC p95 (otelconnect) vs browser p95
panels.description: Browser minus server = queueing + network + socket + encode; a wide gap points at the transport, not the handler.

links.title: Slow server RPC spans (> 500ms) in Tempo (Explore)

panels.title: Slow browser spans (stapler-squad-web, > 1s)
panels.description: Browser fetch/document-load spans from the OTLP relay (needs NEXT_PUBLIC_OTEL_ENABLED=true web build). Click a trace id to open it in Tempo; the browser traceparent links to the server span.

panels.title: Slow server RPC spans for the selected methods (> 500ms, streams excluded)
panels.description: Server-side Connect handler spans for the selected RPC method(s). Compare with the browser view above: a slow browser call with no slow server span points at queuing or the transport, not the handler. Click a trace id to open it in Tempo.

targets.query: { resource.service.name = "stapler-squad" && span.rpc.system = "connect_rpc" && kind = server && span.rpc.method =~ "(${method:pipe})" && name !~ ".*Watch.*" && duration > 500ms }

panels.title: Errored server RPC spans for the selected methods
panels.description: Server-side Connect handler spans with status=error for the selected RPC method(s).

targets.query: { resource.service.name = "stapler-squad" && span.rpc.system = "connect_rpc" && kind = server && span.rpc.method =~ "(${method:pipe})" && name !~ ".*Watch.*" && status = error }
